optimizedCVData.summary: Backend engineer with 11 years of experience designing and operating high-throughput payment and event-processing services in Java, Kotlin, and Python. Built and ran a Kotlin settlement service processing approximately 40 million Kafka events per day, and reduced p99 API latency by 75% through targeted caching with Redis. Experienced in leading cross-functional engineering teams, driving monolith-to-microservices migrations, and maintaining production systems at scale on AWS. Returning to full-time engineering after a planned family caregiving break, during which AWS certification and active open-source contributions kept skills current.

bullets: Designed and operated the settlement service in Kotlin and Spring Boot, processing approximately 40 million events per day on Kafka with high reliability across the payments platform.
Cut p99 latency of the payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, improving end-user experience for a high-traffic financial product.
Led a team of 4 engineers through a 9-month migration from a monolith to 6 independent services, coordinating delivery across backend, infrastructure, and QA stakeholders.
Served as on-call engineer for the payments platform and authored post-incident reviews for 14 incidents, improving system observability and team response processes.
Built order and inventory services in Java and Spring, backed by PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, supporting retail transaction processing at scale.
Introduced contract testing practices that reduced integration bugs found in staging by approximately one third, improving release confidence across the engineering team.
Contributed to API design and service boundary decisions as the team transitioned toward a more modular backend architecture.
Completed AWS Solutions Architect Associate preparation coursework and earned the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate certification (2024) to maintain cloud infrastructure knowledge.
Participated in a reading group covering Designing Data-Intensive Applications and contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library to stay active in the engineering community.
Delivered internal web tools for two client engagements using Java and JavaScript, gaining foundational experience in backend development and client-facing delivery.

Hiring Manager
Duolingo

Dear Hiring Manager,

Designing a settlement service that processed tens of millions of events daily on Kafka taught me that scalable backend systems live or die by the decisions made long before the first line of code ships. That kind of ownership is exactly what Duolingo's backend engineering teams need as they scale services across half a billion learners.

At Lumen Payments, I built and operated high-throughput services in Kotlin, Java, and Spring Boot, cutting payment API latency by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis and leading a nine-month monolith-to-microservices migration across a team of four engineers. I also bring production experience with Datadog for observability and AWS (EC2, RDS, SQS, S3) for cloud infrastructure, which maps directly to Duolingo's expectation that engineers take ownership of complex problems from design through production. Working cross-functionally with product and data science teams was a regular part of my role, so the collaboration model your Ads and AI Platform teams describe is familiar ground.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my backend experience translates to Duolingo's engineering challenges. I am available for a conversation at your convenience.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
